coupling: The decode-parameter commit first consolidates the two four-byte smhd reads into one read of the full atom payload size and reads the balance field from its original second-word offset. That commit is safe because decodeBlock still resizes buf to the payload size before tagDecoder runs. The later resize-removal commit removes that expansion and leaves a fixed five-byte DataBuf; on its own, the original two-read smhd consumer remains bounded, but composed with the earlier size-based read it writes an eight-byte smhd payload into five bytes. The string-termination commit keeps the QuickTime brand lookup bounded so ImageFactory::open accepts the in-contract input and reaches the composed parser path. A reviewer must reason across the commits: the size-based read depends on capacity supplied by decodeBlock, while the resize removal is only unsafe because of that consumer. A correct durable fix must either restore payload-aware capacity in decodeBlock or allocate/bound the payload read in tagDecoder; changing only the cosmetic buffer simplification or brand lookup does not address the capacity dependency.
